transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because things at work have been getting scary. In the middle of service I’ll just freeze up, or do things out of order. Like I stood by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, repeating table numbers instead of closing the checks. Everybody noticed.
Do you remember what happened while you were doing that, or did someone have to tell you about it afterward?
I remember it. I was just standing there with the cash drawer key, repeating the table numbers, even though I knew I was supposed to be closing checks. I kind of froze and got the steps mixed up.
When you were repeating those table numbers and froze, did you feel a strong urge or need to say them, or did your body just freeze against your will?

It didn’t feel like I had to say the numbers. I just sort of froze there, holding the key, and then I was repeating them instead of doing the checks. Like I couldn’t get myself back into the right order.
Right before you freeze up like this, do you notice any unusual sensations, like a rising feeling in your stomach, a strange smell, or a sense of déjà vu?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that beforehand. It just seems to happen suddenly—I’ll realize I’m stuck once I’m already doing it.
Have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people don't seem to hear or see?

Sometimes I hear a woman’s voice, usually when I’m closing at work or at home in the kitchen. She’ll say my name, or tell me I’m doing the count wrong. It sounds clear enough that I’ll answer her before I realize nobody else heard anything.
Do you have any medical conditions, or have you had any recent physical illnesses?
I’m not really sure what would count, but I haven’t had any recent physical illness that I know of.
Have you felt like people are watching you, spying on you, or trying to harm you in any way?

Yeah. I keep feeling like a couple of the other servers, and this one regular customer, are watching how I ring things in. Like they leave little signs on the tickets to show they’re trying to get me fired. My husband says it’s just normal restaurant mistakes, but it doesn’t feel like that to me.
Have you ever found yourself holding awkward or unnatural body positions for long periods of time?

Not really holding a pose, but I have frozen up at work. I’ll just stand by the soda station with the cash drawer key in my hand, repeating table numbers instead of closing the checks. It scared everybody because I was doing things all out of order.
Has anyone ever tried to move your limbs or body while you were frozen like that, and if so, what happened?
No, I don’t think anyone tried to move me. They were mostly scared because I was just standing there holding the drawer key, repeating table numbers instead of closing the checks.
Do you ever find yourself repeating words or phrases that other people around you have just said?
I don’t think I repeat what other people say. It’s more that I get stuck repeating the table numbers to myself, like when I’m supposed to be closing checks.
Do you ever find yourself automatically copying or mimicking the body movements or gestures of people around you?
No, I haven’t noticed myself copying other people’s movements or gestures.
When you freeze up like that, are you able to speak to people if they try to talk to you?

Sometimes I don’t answer right away. At work I’ve just stood there by the soda station holding the drawer key, repeating table numbers instead of doing the checks. People were talking to me, but I was kind of stuck on the numbers.
When people ask you to do something or try to guide you, do you ever find yourself resisting them or doing the complete opposite for no clear reason?

I don’t know if I’m trying to resist them. It’s more like I freeze up or do things out of order. I’ll be standing there with the cash drawer key, repeating table numbers, when I’m supposed to be closing checks. It scared everyone at work.
Have you ever experienced sudden periods of intense, frantic physical activity or restlessness that seemed purposeless and completely out of control?
No, I don’t think I’ve had anything like that. I haven’t noticed myself getting suddenly really active or restless for no reason.
When you freeze up like that, do your muscles feel stiff or rigid to the point that it's difficult to move them?

It’s not really that my muscles feel stiff. I just sort of stop in the middle of things and get stuck doing the wrong thing—like holding the drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing checks.
